experimental_procedure: Ethyl 2-[(2-ethoxy-2-oxoethoxy)methyl]quinoline-3-carboxylate (II) Ethyl 2-hydroxyacetate (10.4 g, 100 mmol) was added dropwise over 5 min to a stirred solution of sodium ethoxide (3.74 g, 55 mmol) in absolute ethanol (30 mL) and the reaction mixture was stirred at 50°C for 5 h. The solvent was evaporated and the resulting sodium salt of ethyl 2-hydroxyacetate (a white solid) was added to a solution of I (14.7 g, 50 mmol) in anhydrous benzene (22 mL) and heated under reflux for 10 h (monitored by TLC). The reaction was quenched with water and the product was extracted with Et2O. The organic layer was dried with anhydrous Na2SO4, filtered and the solvent evaporated to give the crude product; this was then purified by flash chromatography on a column of silica gel (100-200 mesh) using petroleum ether/EtOAc (ϕr = 10 : 1) as the eluent to afford II. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General method for the synthesis of 2-aryloxy-N,N-diethyletanamine hydrochlorides. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: PREPARATION OF PHENOXIDE Phenol and substituted phenols (1 mmol) were dissolved in aqueous sodium hydroxide solution (1.2 mmol) and stirred for 2 h at room-temperature. Water was evaporated under reduced pressure to get solid phenoxides. PREPARATION OF DIARYLOXYMETHANES A mixture of phenoxides (2 mmol) and dichloromethane (1 mmol) was stirred in ionic liquid [bmim] Br (5 mL) at 60°C for an appropriate time period as shown in Table 2. Completion of the reaction was monitored by thin-layer chromatography using 5% ethyl acetate in petroleum ether. The reaction mixture was diluted with water (20 mL) and then extracted with ethyl acetate (3 x 10 mL). The separated organic layer was dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate, and the solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure to afford the diaryloxymethanes. The product was purified by column chromatography using 5% ethyl acetate in petroleum ether as an eluent. The ionic liquid was extracted from the aqueous layer with dichloromethane (3 x 10 mL) and dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate, and the solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure leaving behind the ionic liquid [bmim] Br, which could be recycled. After stirring at room temperature for 1h, silica gel (~ 200 mg) is added, and solvent is removed under reduced pressure. The preabsorbed reaction mixture is chrornatographed through a column of silica gel (EtOAc/hexanes) to give the alcohols 4 as clear, colorless oils. experimental_procedure: General method for the synthesis of 2-aryloxy-N,N-diethyletanamine hydrochlorides. A mixture of 0.1 mole of the corresponding phenol. 70 ml toluene, 0.1 mole of hydrochloride or hydrobromide (2-chloro- or 2-bromo-, respectively) of N,N-diethylethanamine, and 12.5 g of comminuted NaOH was boiled with stirring for 8 h on a sand bath, cooled, alkalized with a NaOH solution until obtaining an alkaline reaction, and extracted with ether (150 ml). The ether - toluene extract was washed with NaOH solution until complete discoloration of the aqueous phase. The organic layer was dried over crystalline NaOH and filtered. The filtrate was purged with dry HCl and the precipitated 2-aryloxy-N,N-diethyletanamine hydrochloride was separated by filtration, washed with ether, and crystallized from an appropriate solvent. In cases where no solvent for crystallization can be found, the product is purified by converting it onto the base form and repeated purging with dry HCl. Compound I, yield 81.8%. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Preparation of 2-Ethoxy-3-(4-benzyloxyphenyl)-propionic Acid Isopropyl Ester (11c). The isolated 10c (105 g, 0.334 mol) was placed in an inerted 6 L reactor and dissolved in anhydrous DMF (1 L, 2O). The resulting solution was cooled to -30 °C and treated with ethyl iodide (261 g, 1.674 mol). This homogeneous mixture was subsequently treated with a solution of sodium tert-amylate in toluene (420 mL, 0.42 mol, 1 M solution) at such a rate that the temperature was maintained between -27 to -30 °C. After addition of approximately three-fourths of the total charge of base, a precipitate formed that caused an increase in the internal temperature, requiring a decrease in the addition rate to maintain the prescribed temperature. After 1.5 h of stirring at -30 °C, an in-process assay indicated 6% of 10c still remained. An additional portion of 1 M sodium tert-amylate (30 mL, 0.03 mol) was added, and the reaction mixture was stirred for an additional l h. Acetic acid (32.5 g, 1.54 mol) was added dropwise, and the mixture was warmed to ca. 10 °C. Toluene (2 L) was added followed by water (1 L), added at 10 °C (exothermic dissolution of the solids caused a temperature increase up to 22 °C). The organic layer was separated, and the aqueous layer was diluted with an additional 0.5 L of water and re-extracted by 0.5 L toluene. The combined organic layers are washed twice with 0.5 L of water followed by 15% NaCl solution (0.5 L). The toluene was evaporated under reduced pressure to afford crude 11c (ca 130 g). The crude material was then purified on silica gel (330 g) using cyclohexane/ethyl acetate (90/10 v/v) as the eluent. Purified 11c was isolated as a pale yellow oil in 90% yield (122.8 g, 0.3 mol). experimental_procedure: Preparation of S-2-Ethoxy-3-[4-(R-1-carboxy-ethoxy)- phenyl]-propionic Acid Isopropyl Ester (2c). The starting material 4c (99.84 g, 395.7 mmol, 1.0 equiv) was azeotropically dried from toluene and added as a solution in anhydrous THF (2 L). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General method for the synthesis of 2-aryloxy-N,N-diethyletanamine hydrochlorides. A mixture of 0.1 mole of the corresponding phenol. 70 ml toluene, 0.1 mole of hydrochloride or hydrobromide (2-chloro- or 2-bromo-, respectively) of N,N-diethylethanamine, and 12.5 g of comminuted NaOH was boiled with stirring for 8 h on a sand bath, cooled, alkalized with a NaOH solution until obtaining an alkaline reaction, and extracted with ether (150 ml). The ether - toluene extract was washed with NaOH solution until complete discoloration of the aqueous phase. The organic layer was dried over crystalline NaOH and filtered. The filtrate was purged with dry HCl and the precipitated 2-aryloxy-N,N-diethyletanamine hydrochloride was separated by filtration, washed with ether, and crystallized from an appropriate solvent. In cases where no solvent for crystallization can be found, the product is purified by converting it onto the base form and repeated purging with dry HCl. Compound X, yield 74.2%. title: Synthesis and antimicrobial activity of 2-aryloxy-N,N-diethylethanamine derivatives
authors: Semenovykh, E. V.; Pantsurkin, V. I.; Novikova, V. V.; Odegova, T. F.; Syropyatov, B. Ya.; Vakhrin, M. I.
reference: Synthesis and antimicrobial activity of 2-aryloxy-N,N-diethylethanamine derivatives | Semenovykh, E. V.; Pantsurkin, V. I.; Novikova, V. V.; Odegova, T. F.; Syropyatov, B. Ya.; Vakhrin, M. I. | Pharmaceutical Chemistry Journal (2007), 41(4), 211-215
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General method for the synthesis of 2-aryloxy-N,N-diethyletanamine hydrochlorides. A mixture of 0.1 mole of the corresponding phenol. 70 ml toluene, 0.1 mole of hydrochloride or hydrobromide (2-chloro- or 2-bromo-, respectively) of N,N-diethylethanamine, and 12.5 g of comminuted NaOH was boiled with stirring for 8 h on a sand bath, cooled, alkalized with a NaOH solution until obtaining an alkaline reaction, and extracted with ether (150 ml). The ether - toluene extract was washed with NaOH solution until complete discoloration of the aqueous phase. The organic layer was dried over crystalline NaOH and filtered. The filtrate was purged with dry HCl and the precipitated 2-aryloxy-N,N-diethyletanamine hydrochloride was separated by filtration, washed with ether, and crystallized from an appropriate solvent. In cases where no solvent for crystallization can be found, the product is purified by converting it onto the base form and repeated purging with dry HCl. Compound IV, yield 91.4%. Empirical formula: C13H21NO2.HCl; M.p. 116 - 118°C (toluene); 1H NMR δ, ppm (CDCl3): 1.354 t (6H, N(CH2CH3)2), 3.07 - 3.40 m (6H, CH2N(CH2CH3)2), 3.715 s (3H, 2-OCH3), 4.354 t (2H, OCH2CH2), 6.74 - 6.82 m (4H, arom. experimental_procedure: Experimental Section Key Intermediate (4) Synthesis. A quantity of 6.48 mmol (1.50 g) of allyl 2,3-O-isopropylidene-R-D-lyxofuranoside was coevaporated twice with anhydrous toluene and left under high vacuum for 2 h in the presence of activated molecular sieves (0.4 nm). Under Ar atmosphere, 8.43 mmol (5.09 g) of 2,3,4,6-tetra-O-benzyl-Dgalactopyranosyl Dgalactopyranosyl bromide,12 dissolved in 65 mL of anhydrous dichloromethane, was added, giving a colorless solution; 19.45 mmol (5.00 g, 4.46 mL) of tri(1-pyrrolidine)phosphine oxide was added dropwise, and the reaction was stirred under Ar atmosphere for 24 h at room temperature. Solution was diluted with AcOEt and filtered on a plug of Celite. The crude obtained after evaporation of the solvent was purified by flash chromatography to give 4.12 g of pure allyl 2,3,4,6-tetra-O-benzyl-R-D-galactopyranosyl-(1f5)-2,3-O-isopropylidene-R-D-lyxofuranoside 3 in 84% yield. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: 4-(4-Methoxyphenyl)-7-(2-oxopropoxy)-2H-2-chromenone (7). A hot solution of 5 (1.07 g, 4 mmole) in absolute acetone (30 mL) was treated with freshly calcined potash (1.66 g, 12 mmole), stirred vigorously and heated (50-56°C), and treated with chloroacetone (0.35 mL, 4.4 mmole). The reaction mixture was left for 1 h with heating and vigorous stirring (completion of the reaction determined by TLC). The reaction mixture was poured into H2SO4 solution (300 mL, I N). The resulting precipitate was filtered off and crystallized from propan-2-ol. 7-(2-(4-Fluorophenyl)-2-oxoethoxy]-4-(4-methoxyphenyl)-8-methyl-2H-2-chromenone (20). Prepared analogously to 7 from 6 (1.13 g, 4 mmole) and 4-fluorophenacylchloride (0.72 g, 4.2 mmole). Yield 1.56 g (93%). C25H19FO5, mp 199-200°C. IR spectrum (KBr, cm-1): 1714, 1699, 1611, 1514, 1427, 1371, 1299, 1261, 1243, 1233, 1181, 1133, 1029, 835. UV spectrum (CH3CN, λmax, nm, log ε): 203 (4.84), 240 (4.37), 310 (4.27). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: PREPARATION OF PHENOXIDE Phenol and substituted phenols (1 mmol) were dissolved in aqueous sodium hydroxide solution (1.2 mmol) and stirred for 2 h at room-temperature. Water was evaporated under reduced pressure to get solid phenoxides. PREPARATION OF DIARYLOXYMETHANES A mixture of phenoxides (2 mmol) and dichloromethane (1 mmol) was stirred in ionic liquid [bmim] Br (5 mL) at 60°C for an appropriate time period as shown in Table 2. Completion of the reaction was monitored by thin-layer chromatography using 5% ethyl acetate in petroleum ether. The reaction mixture was diluted with water (20 mL) and then extracted with ethyl acetate (3 x 10 mL). The separated organic layer was dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate, and the solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure to afford the diaryloxymethanes. The product was purified by column chromatography using 5% ethyl acetate in petroleum ether as an eluent. The ionic liquid was extracted from the aqueous layer with dichloromethane (3 x 10 mL) and dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate, and the solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure leaving behind the ionic liquid [bmim] Br, which could be recycled. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: PREPARATION OF PHENOXIDE Phenol and substituted phenols (1 mmol) were dissolved in aqueous sodium hydroxide solution (1.2 mmol) and stirred for 2 h at room-temperature. Water was evaporated under reduced pressure to get solid phenoxides. PREPARATION OF DIARYLOXYMETHANES A mixture of phenoxides (2 mmol) and dichloromethane (1 mmol) was stirred in ionic liquid [bmim] Br (5 mL) at 60°C for an appropriate time period as shown in Table 2. Completion of the reaction was monitored by thin-layer chromatography using 5% ethyl acetate in petroleum ether. The reaction mixture was diluted with water (20 mL) and then extracted with ethyl acetate (3 x 10 mL). The separated organic layer was dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate, and the solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure to afford the diaryloxymethanes. The product was purified by column chromatography using 5% ethyl acetate in petroleum ether as an eluent. The ionic liquid was extracted from the aqueous layer with dichloromethane (3 x 10 mL) and dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate, and the solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure leaving behind the ionic liquid [bmim] Br, which could be recycled. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General method for the synthesis of 2-aryloxy-N,N-diethyletanamine hydrochlorides. A mixture of 0.1 mole of the corresponding phenol. 70 ml toluene, 0.1 mole of hydrochloride or hydrobromide (2-chloro- or 2-bromo-, respectively) of N,N-diethylethanamine, and 12.5 g of comminuted NaOH was boiled with stirring for 8 h on a sand bath, cooled, alkalized with a NaOH solution until obtaining an alkaline reaction, and extracted with ether (150 ml). The ether - toluene extract was washed with NaOH solution until complete discoloration of the aqueous phase. The organic layer was dried over crystalline NaOH and filtered.
